title: fix(rest): `GET /data/:object/export` honours a `search` term
body:
Found while auditing objectui's `ListView` export path (objectui#3072 follow-up).

## The bug

The streaming export route accepted `filter` and `orderby` but had **no way to carry the search term**. A user who searched a list and then exported downloaded the *unsearched superset* — more rows than the screen showed, in a file that looks authoritative, with nothing anywhere indicating the difference.

The route's own comment claimed the opposite:

> Mirrors the active view's filter + sort so the exported file matches what the user sees.

It mirrored the *filter* half. There was no field for the other half — objectui's `ExportDownloadRequest` had no `search` either, so the client couldn't have sent one.

Same family as a dropped filter (#3948, #4181): a plausible answer that is quietly broader than the one asked for.

## The change

Two query params, both matching the list endpoint's semantics:

| param | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `search=<term>` | folded into `findData` as `$search`, so it **composes** with `filter` (`{ $and: [filter, search] }`) rather than replacing it. Empty / whitespace-only terms are ignored, not applied as a blank predicate. |
| `searchFields=a,b` | ADR-0061 override for which fields the term scans. Only meaningful alongside `search`; the engine intersects it with the object's allowed searchable set, exactly as on the list endpoint. |

**Backward compatible in both directions.** Unknown query params on this route were already ignored, so a client that sends `search` to an older server gets today's behaviour rather than an error — which means the objectui side can land independently.

## Verification

Real engine + real protocol + in-memory driver (`export-integration.test.ts`), no protocol mocks.

The composition test is built so **each half alone returns a different non-empty result, and only "both applied" returns none** — `filter: done=true` → `写代码`, `search: 文档` → `写文档`, together → 0 rows. A test where the two halves agree would have passed just as well with `search` dropped entirely; I wrote that weaker version first and it survived the revert check, so it was replaced.

**Reverting `rest-server.ts` fails 4 of the tests.** Full `@objectstack/rest` suite: 35 files / 519 tests green.

The file's in-memory driver also learned `$or` / `$contains`. `$search` folds to `{ $or: [{ field: { $contains: term } }] }`, and this driver skipped `$`-prefixed keys — so it returned every row regardless, and an "it filtered" assertion would have passed for the wrong reason.

## Note

`packages/rest/src/package-routes.ts` has two pre-existing `TS2345` errors on `main` (verified against a clean tree). Untouched here.

Refs #3948, #4181, objectui#3072
